title: Permission orthogonalization and timeline-anchored scopes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define and land a role model that treats permissions as orthogonal axes (action, resource-slice, temporal scope, and context tags) and a migration path from the current monolithic role blobs to a composable, auditable RBAC v2.

Why now: current permission surface makes it hard to reason about cross-tenant admin grants, temporary breakglass, and API keys with scoped least privilege. This ticket scopes the design and an initial implementation for (a) resource hierarchy anchoring, (b) timeline-anchored scopes (time-bound elevations and canary windows), (c) a compact permissions matrix that can be evaluated cheaply in the request path, and (d) audit tagging to preserve provenance for every effective grant.

Outcomes expected:
- A machine-parseable role schema with explicit axes: action (read/write/admin), resource_slice (project, dataset, runtime-pool), temporal_scope (permanent|ephemeral|canary-window), context_tags (delegation_origin, sso_assertion_id).
- Migration helpers: role diff tooling, shadow-evaluation mode, and an automated migration playbook for early adopter orgs.
- Integration points: SSO/SAML attribute mapping instructions (for group->role derivation), audit log enrichment hooks (request-level grant_ids), and admin console controls for creating time-bound grants.

Non-goals: full UI polish for Console; complete tenant admin delegation UX (iterative follow-ups will handle).

Notes on evaluation model: decision is to evaluate permissions at request ingress with a small, precomputed "effective-grant" cache keyed by principal+resource-prefix+temporal-bucket. Cache invalidation will be driven by grant lifecycle events and SSO assertion revocation hooks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Role schema document accepted by Security and Platform leads; 2) Prototype service-side evaluator that returns allow/deny with grant provenance ID; 3) Shadow evaluation demonstrates 0 false-deny for 7-day sampled production traffic; 4) Audit log events include grant_id, evaluated_axes, and SSO assertion id when present; 5) Console can create a time-bound grant via the admin API (no UI required).
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): implement evaluator behind feature flag and run shadow-eval on 5% of traffic for two weeks; Phase B (limited write rollout): enable time-bound grants in Console for security team and two pilot customers; Phase C (migration tooling): provide CLI to translate common legacy roles and a 1-click shadow->enforce toggle for pilot orgs; Phase D: full enforcement and telemetry-based fallback policy if we detect >0.1% new denial rate post-enforcement.
migration_strategy:
1) Produce a role translator that emits v2 role axes from existing role blobs; 2) Run translator in read-only mode and produce a mapping table; 3) Shadow-evaluate translated grants alongside legacy model for at least 7 days with alerting for mismatches; 4) For mismatches, create temporary exception grants and iterate; 5) After stabilization, flip enforcement per-org using migration CLI.

Backwards compatibility: keep legacy resolver in codebase for 6 months post-rollout; deprecation schedule to be announced when 90%+ of orgs have migrated or opted in.
comments: 2026-03-13 Maya Chen: Kickoff - drafted initial schema and shared with Security. Key design point: prefer allow-list semantics but add explicit deny overrides for emergency breakglass. Open question: should deny overrides be prioritized entirely or only within same resource scope?

2026-03-13 Arjun Patel: Implementing evaluator prototype. Chose a compact bitmask representation for action axes to keep per-request cost low. Prototype passes synthetic perf test: 95th percentile eval time 220µs. Will instrument shadow-eval next.

2026-03-14 Lina Gómez (Security): Reviewed schema. Requested: SSO/SAML mapping matrix examples for Okta and Azure AD and clear guidance on group-to-role precedence. Also asked to include assertion_id in logs for forensic linking. Marked security review required.

2026-03-14 Prashant Rao (Platform): Concern about cache invalidation storms when many short-lived grants are created. Suggested grouping ephemeral grants into 1-minute temporal buckets to reduce churn. Agreed to simulate before finalizing.
2026-03-14 Arjun Patel: Added temporal-bucket approach to design and updated prototype to bucket ephemeral grants. Running load tests to validate invalidation rates.
notes: Trade-offs considered: precompute effective grants (fast reads, more write complexity) vs compute-on-read (simpler writes, higher read latency). Chosen: precompute + efficient invalidation for predictable SLOs.
Testing plan: unit tests for evaluator, integration tests with SSO assertion replay (sample Okta SAML assertions), end-to-end shadow-eval on production mirror traffic, and chaos test for grant churn.
Follow-ups: UI design ticket for console grant UX (PM to own), metrics alerting for 'shadow mismatch rate', and a compliance playbook for audit exports.
